pains.label: My score is stuck or going down no matter how much I study
pains.definition: The person has prepared for weeks or months and the practice or real score is flat or falling. Plateau posts, 'why is my score not improving', 'scores keep decreasing'.

pains.label: I scored lower on the real test than on my practice tests
pains.definition: The real exam felt harder than PowerPrep or third-party mocks, or the person crumbled under pressure and the official score came in well below practice scores.

pains.label: Quant: careless mistakes, running out of time, can't reach 170, or no maths background
pains.definition: Trouble with the quantitative section itself: silly errors, timing, the last few points to 170, or coming from a non-maths background.

pains.label: Verbal, vocabulary and reading comprehension are hard, especially when English is not my first language
pains.definition: Trouble with the verbal section: word lists, reading comprehension, text completion, and the extra burden for non-native speakers.

pains.label: Which prep is worth paying for: coaching or self-study, Magoosh or GregMat, a tutor, a class I can't afford
pains.definition: The person must decide what to spend on: coaching institute vs self-study, which subscription or course, whether a tutor is worth it, what coaching costs, or how to prepare cheaply because they cannot afford a class.

pains.label: The exam fee, retakes and extra score reports cost too much
pains.definition: Complaints and questions about the ETS fee itself (about $220 to $249, Rs 22,000 in India), the cost of a second attempt, rescheduling charges, and paying for extra score reports.

pains.label: I cancelled and can't get my refund; ETS or the prep company won't answer
pains.definition: The person cancelled a test or a subscription and is chasing the money: refund not received for months or years, unclear refund policy, no reply from support.

pains.label: The at-home test went wrong: internet, proctor, software, test ended early
pains.definition: Technical or proctoring trouble with the GRE at home: lost connection, the session ending early, delays, flags, uncertainty about whether the score will stand.

pains.label: ETS put my scores on hold or cancelled them after the test
pains.definition: Scores unavailable, on hold, or cancelled by ETS after the test (often the at-home edition), with no clear reason or remedy.

pains.label: My score is short: should I retake, how many times can I, and will it improve
pains.definition: Deciding whether to sit again after a disappointing score, how often retakes are allowed, whether a retake will really add points, and how to prepare for it in 21 days.

pains.label: Is my score enough for the programs I want, and does a low score sink my application
pains.definition: Not knowing what score a program needs, whether a low score kills an MS or PhD application, and how to shortlist universities with the score in hand.

pains.label: Not enough time: a full-time job, or the test is only days or weeks away
pains.definition: Preparing alongside a full-time job, or with a month, three weeks or ten days left, and needing a plan that fits.

pains.label: Test anxiety, panic on the day, burnout during prep
pains.definition: Stress and fear around the exam: freezing on test day, a 'nightmare' session, burnout from months of study.

pains.label: Do I need the GRE at all: test-optional programs, GMAT instead, is it a waste of money
pains.definition: Unsure whether to sit the GRE now that many programs are test-optional, whether the GMAT is the better choice, or whether the whole exam is a waste of money.

pains.label: I've run out of realistic or hard practice questions and official mock tests
pains.definition: Wanting harder or more realistic questions than the usual books, asking which platform's questions resemble the real exam, and rationing the few official ETS tests.

pains.label: I don't know how to start, what to use, or how long to study
pains.definition: Beginners asking how to prepare, where to start, which sources to use, and how many weeks or months to plan for.
